body:
Owning issue: https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/387
Owner requested parallel implementation on 2026-09-30. Original issue intent follows; repository contracts and accepted authority remain governing.

## Summary

`go run ./tools/qualify-opencode` (commit `25730ea`, OpenCode 2.0.19 on darwin/arm64) passed only on the third of three consecutive runs on the same machine. It then keeps OpenCode `UNQUALIFIED` until a manual retry. The two failures had different causes:

1. **Focused gate:** `TestHostAdapterJavaScriptHosts/GOC-V0-008…` failed in `integrations/host-adapters.test.mjs:101` (`CRB-V0-012 OpenCode exact transport, unicode bounds, receipt and env`) with `assert.equal(result.ok, true)`: `false !== true` after about 2017 ms. The machine was busy (a Docker lane reset was running), which suggests a fixed ~2 s bound on the fixture round trip.
2. **Native cleanup gate** (next run, machine idle): `observed command cleanup incomplete` listed three processes (`PPID 53543`, started during the run). They had exited by the time I inspected them a minute later, which suggests a race between the 20 ms observer and child exit.

Run 3, with nothing else changed, passed all 14 conformance groups.

## Request

- Make both bounds robust under ordinary load: an adaptive or longer deadline for the CRB-V0-012 round trip, and a short settle or retry window before declaring cleanup incomplete, while still failing on true survivors.
- Or have the tool report a transient/retryable classification distinct from a real failure, so wrappers can retry safely.

## Why it matters

The qualification record is bound to the exact `corvint` binary, so every source update needs a new run. Flaky runs silently drop an otherwise working host integration to `UNQUALIFIED`.

## Environment

macOS 26.7 arm64, Go 1.27.1, Node 24.11.1, OpenCode 2.0.19, Corvint `main` `25730ea`.
title: GH #387: qualify-opencode is timing-sensitive: CRB-V0-012 round trip and cleanup observer fail intermittently
